Authentication Course Overview

Authentication Training Journey

Start with Spring Boot and a Java JWT auth server. Learn how protected services validate tokens. Cross into JavaScript and TypeScript. Then build the replacement auth service in NestJS, secure it with bcrypt and testing, and finish by documenting the whole API with Swagger.

Start the Journey View Course Modules
Core stack Spring Boot → NestJS
Security skills BCrypt, JWTs, Validation
Language path Java → JavaScript → TypeScript
Finish line Testing, Swagger, Deployment-readiness
Wax On. Wipe Off. Build for Real.

Train the fundamentals until secure habits feel automatic

This section is organized like skill training. Every lesson adds another motion: store users safely, hash passwords, sign tokens, validate claims, understand modern backend JavaScript, build a Node-based auth service, test it, and expose a clean API contract. The goal is not just to know the pieces, but to practice them until they fit together naturally.

Build secure APIs

Understand password storage, token verification, protected endpoints, DTO validation and safer logging practices.

Work across stacks

Follow the story from Java and Spring into JavaScript, TypeScript and NestJS without losing the core security concepts.

Learn by connected pages

Each lesson is self-contained, but all pages link together so students can move through the sequence like one course.

Finish with a real service

The section ends with a working replacement auth service, focused tests and OpenAPI docs that describe the finished API.

“Wipe On. Wipe Off.” Small repetitions, stronger security.
The course begins with fundamentals and keeps building until the full authentication workflow feels natural.
Practice creates muscle memory. Repeated small skills add up: DTO validation, careful logging, bcrypt hashing, signing JWTs, verifying tokens, testing services and documenting endpoints.

Your learning path

From first concepts to a production-ready auth journey

Every module pushes the story forward. The learning path moves from core concepts, to hands-on implementation, to verification, documentation and deployment-minded thinking.

1. Learn core concepts → 2. Build a Java auth server → 3. Validate JWTs → 4. Learn JS and TS → 5. Build NestJS auth → 6. Test and document
Balance. Discipline. Better code. Students leave this section understanding how tokens are created and trusted, how Node and NestJS can replace an earlier auth stub, and how testing plus Swagger bring clarity to the finished service.
